title: Derived restriction of a strict-local neighbourhood germ
statement: Let f, s, K, n, J, q and the canonical comparison A_i be as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-injective-source-comparison], and Q as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-neighbourhood-geometry]. Write ell_i for the canonical source germ leg [def-weil-pbc-canonical-derived-cohomology-germs], m for the derived mate homology map, and T for the target iso [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-mate-projection-data]. For each i, ell_i m T equals A_i c_i followed by the derived cohomology restriction along Q.legs.app i: the inverse-image adjunction unit, derived Leray, and inverse of the inverse-image composition comparison for Q.over i. Here c_i is the canonical representativeSectionsComparison at the stage [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sections-pullback-comparison]. This statement does not identify the derived restriction with termwise restriction or assert acyclicity at the limit.

proof.text: The termwise direct image of the given bounded-below complex of injectives is bounded below and K-injective: the inverse-image left adjoint is exact, so direct image preserves injectives. Use sourceInjectiveDirectImageIso to obtain its specified representative r of Rf_*K.
Apply sourceLocalizedSectionsIso_germ to this representative on S. It factors the canonical source germ leg through cohomology of the actual complex of sections on the neighbourhood.

Apply strictLocalComplexSectionRestriction_mate to identify that base complex restriction followed by the derived mate and target isomorphism with stage sections identification, termwise fibre restriction, and the limit representative sections comparison.

The cone-leg clause of injectiveSections_strictLocal_comparison replaces termwise restriction followed by the limit comparison by the stage comparison followed by derived cohomology restriction. Unfold sourceLocalizedSectionsIso and strictLocalInjectiveSourceIso and reassociate: the localized Hom factors followed by the stage section factors are definitionally the original source isomorphism.
